description: Authoritative registry of tools ai-toolkit integrates with. Consumed by scripts/ecosystem_doctor.py to detect upstream doc/version drift.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 classes A/B: reviewed stable Claude Code 2.1.311 and native teammate startup/shutdown contracts. Corrected readiness guidance and legacy idle reminders; external-import consent remains a user decision. https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.311
tools.status_note: Claude Code auto-discovers native plugin skills, commands, agents, workflows, output styles, themes, hooks, MCP servers, LSP servers, monitors, executables, and root settings. ai-toolkit's primary install emits its existing rules, skills, agents, and hooks; plugin workflows, output styles, themes, monitors, LSP servers, channels, and root plugin settings are recognized class C surfaces that ai-toolkit does not generate. Themes and monitors are experimental, and plugin settings support only agent and subagentStatusLine.

documentation_review.note: Claude Code 2.1.311 retains emitted native contracts. Teammates launched below the trusted repository root can wait for external CLAUDE.md import consent before reading task messages. Orchestration now checks readiness and uses native teammate shutdown; installed legacy idle reminders migrate without changing user hooks or permissions.

tools.status_note: Claude Chat/Desktop/Cowork does not scan ~/.claude/rules, CLAUDE.md, or Claude Code's user settings, so skills, agents, hooks, and rules ship only as an uploadable plugin ZIP plus Cowork global instructions. Local MCP servers are the exception: the app reads claude_desktop_config.json directly, so `ai-toolkit mcp install --editor claude-app --scope global` configures them without a plugin. That file accepts stdio entries only; HTTP/SSE templates are bridged through mcp-remote. Skills work in Chat and Cowork; plugin hooks and sub-agents run only in Cowork.

documentation_review.note: Plugin ZIP distribution remains compatible. Skills and commands work in Chat; hooks and subagents run in Cowork and Claude Code. Account plugins sync to Claude Code 2.1.273+, so duplicate local/account installs require diagnosis rather than automatic removal. Additional organization/UI features remain optional.

tools.status_note: Cursor 3.11 adds cloud-agent conversation hooks. ai-toolkit emits the complete documented version-1 event set and a self-contained repository runtime under .cursor/hooks/ai-toolkit/; project hook commands do not depend on user-level ~/.cursor or ~/.softspark paths. User entries are preserved and legacy _source-tagged toolkit entries are migrated to schema-valid command ownership markers.

documentation_review.note: The generated version-1 hook event set and custom-agent name/description/model fields remain documented. Agents retain model: inherit; optional per-model parameter syntax does not authorize changing configured models. Existing workspaceOpen observation remains supported without adopting plugin discovery.

tools.status_note: Windsurf rebranded to Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02. .devin/ is the primary rules/workflows/hooks tree; legacy .windsurf rules remain a read fallback. Cascade and its .windsurf/hooks.json format ended on 2026-07-01, so ai-toolkit now emits only .devin/hooks.v1.json. Current Devin skill docs list project .agents/skills, .devin/skills and .windsurf/skills, and user ~/.agents/skills, ~/.config/devin/skills and ~/.codeium/<channel>/skills; ai-toolkit emits a single canonical pointer under .windsurf/skills and no longer also writes .devin/skills. Devin CLI also imports ~/.claude/settings.json hooks when read_config_from.claude is enabled.

documentation_review.note: Native lifecycle hooks and .devin/hooks.v1.json remain compatible. Official skill discovery still includes .windsurf/skills alongside .devin/skills and .agents/skills; retain the single emitted pointer. This contract review is separate from installed or latest Desktop version observations.

Generated command hooks remain compatible. userPromptTransformed is recognized as a documented event but has no toolkit handler. Direct exec/args, agent-scoped hooks, HTTP/prompt handlers and progress messages are optional surfaces, not emitted. The dedicated toolkit hook file does not validate sibling user hook files. Retired infer is already replaced by invocation controls.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 class A: reviewed stable release 0.65.0 (published 2026-10-20), separately from the local version probe. Runtime, authentication and resume fixes require no emitted-config migration. https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/releases/tag/v0.65.0
tools.status_note: Gemini CLI drops free + paid (AI Pro/Ultra) tiers on 2026-06-18 in favor of the new Antigravity CLI (we ship generate_antigravity.py); enterprise Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise keeps full Gemini CLI support. Profile full now emits project and user-tier native agents. Gemini extension export remains class C / not adopted; extension manifests live at the package root and installed extensions live under ~/.gemini/extensions/<name>/.

documentation_review.note: The eleven documented hook events match the generator allowlist; AfterAgent remains the completion event rather than a Claude-style Stop handler. Stable release 0.65.0 fixes runtime/authentication/resume behavior without requiring a generator migration.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 classes A/C: reviewed release 4.1.26 (published 2026-10-26). Cloud-session and provider/runtime changes do not require a generated-config migration; explicit user model selections remain unchanged. https://github.com/cline/cline/releases/tag/v4.1.26

documentation_review.note: The emitted .cline/skills path is recommended and .clinerules/skills remains supported. .clineignore deprecation does not affect toolkit output. Upstream extension hook documentation still marks TaskComplete and PreCompact coming soon, so emitted files alone do not establish those events fire. Plugin/cloud surfaces are optional; release 4.1.26 does not require a generator migration.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 classes A/C: reviewed successor Zoo Code release 3.92.0 (published 2026-10-24), not a Roo binary version observation. Model catalog, lifecycle and UI changes retain the emitted custom-mode contract. https://github.com/Zoo-Code-Org/Zoo-Code/releases/tag/v3.92.0
tools.status_note: Upstream RooCodeInc/Roo-Code archived/read-only 2026-05-15, frozen at v3.54.0. Review the successor Zoo-Code-Org/Zoo-Code (marketplace ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code, docs.zoocode.dev); release 3.92.0 was reviewed on 2026-10-27. Current custom-mode docs explicitly retain JSON .roomodes, and the documented Roo-to-Zoo import accepts exported settings. Emitted .roomodes and .roo/rules contracts remain compatible; this does not establish parity for every product feature. Use Zoo GitHub releases as the authoritative release feed. Global skills use native ~/.agents/skills discovery.

documentation_review.note: Zoo custom modes explicitly retain JSON .roomodes; UI YAML defaults do not deprecate generated JSON. Reviewed Zoo 3.92.0 and the documented Roo-to-Zoo settings import. Model catalog, marketplace and UI changes require no generated-mode migration.

The current options reference retains the emitted architect, read/conventions, lint/test, attribution and commit-language settings. This verifies the configuration contract, not latest-release availability or a local binary version.

Current hook and subagent references retain project/user paths and the native tools allowlist. disabled_tools still overrides tools, including an empty denylist, so the generator correctly omits it. Model inheritance remains the CLI default; no permission expansion or generator migration is needed.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 classes A/C/D: reviewed Antigravity App 2.27.0 (published 2026-10-26), separately from CLI/IDE installations. Workflow retirement is now documented as 2026-10-19; replacement skills already ship. https://antigravity.google/docs/changelog
tools.status_note: Antigravity App 2.27.0 was reviewed on 2026-10-27; earlier CLI/IDE version observations remain historical. Native agent models remain inherit/flash/pro; toolkit agents preserve inherit and validate native tool names. Project skills use .agents/skills/; only .agent/skills/ is legacy. Global skills use ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/ for CLI and ~/.gemini/config/skills/ for the App/IDE shared customization surface. Workflows retired upstream on 2026-10-19; same-named skills preserve the 13 commands, while marked legacy output remains for older clients under issue #34. Native hooks use .agents/hooks.json or ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json; commands resolve from the hooks.json directory. Six events are documented, including SessionStart; the toolkit wires PreToolUse (matcher run_command), PreInvocation and Stop with an adjacent runtime. .agents/rules/*.md need trigger frontmatter; rule files are capped at 24,000 bytes and always-on plus global rules share a 20,000-token budget. Full-profile installs add native subagents. antigravity-plugin remains an opt-in deterministic export. Native MCP output uses serverUrl; legacy url input is normalized and httpUrl is rejected. Unrelated config data is preserved transactionally.

documentation_review.note: Official migration now dates workflow retirement to 2026-10-19. Same-named replacement skills already ship; retain marked legacy output for older clients until a documented removal release under issue #34. Six hook events are documented, including optional SessionStart; only PreToolUse, PreInvocation and Stop are wired. Existing native agent tools and inherit model remain valid.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 classes A/B: reviewed stable Codex 0.164.0 and current native hook/agent/skill/plugin contracts. Fixed SubagentStop JSON, search-first continuation handling and equivalent advisory-hook duplication across layers. Preserve configured models and permissions. https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.164.0

documentation_review.note: Codex 0.164.0 retains native skill/agent/plugin exports. SubagentStop requires JSON; Stop continuations act as user prompts and must not re-arm search. Hook layers are additive, so equivalent toolkit advisory invocations are paired using native identities, with safe fallback when identity is missing. MCP refresh preserves omitted local policies only for unchanged connections. command/mcp_tool hooks execute; prompt/agent remain unsupported. Class B covers corrected native hook handling.

tools.release_review_note: 2026-10-27 classes A/C: reviewed stable OpenCode 1.19.4 (published 2026-10-22), separately from the local version probe. Bundled Bun security updates do not change emitted plugin/agent contracts. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.19.4
tools.status_note: OpenCode's v2 plugin API is beta. Root plugin packages can expose flat skills/*.md and nested skills/**/SKILL.md entries, and config can add local paths or HTTP URLs through the skills array. No migration: the stable JS plugin generator remains unchanged until v2 stabilizes. Note sst/opencode redirects to anomalyco/opencode.

documentation_review.note: Stable JavaScript plugin paths/events and agent permission contracts remain compatible. Deprecated agent tools is already omitted. Release 1.19.4 updates bundled Bun without changing those contracts; optional v2 package surfaces do not require a speculative plugin migration.
